title: Positional Strategy: Engineering Around 'Lost in the Middle' in Long Context + RAG
thesis: Long-context LLMs are not position-robust: the same fact can be ignored or used depending on where it appears. Therefore, context placement and repetition are first-class design parameters (like indexes in databases), especially in RAG and multi-document reasoning.

phenomena.name: lost_in_the_middle
phenomena.what_it_means: Model performance is often highest when relevant info is near the beginning or the end, and degrades when relevant info is placed in the middle.

phenomena.name: more_retrieval_is_not_monotonic
phenomena.what_it_means: In evaluated question-answering tasks, adding more retrieved documents showed diminishing returns; test the choice for the model and task.

phenomena.name: attention_sink
phenomena.what_it_means: Some streaming transformer models show attention sinks at initial tokens. This is a distinct observation from lost-in-the-middle performance; do not assume it explains every positional effect.

phenomena.name: positional_bias_calibration
phenomena.what_it_means: There are methods to mitigate middle-position failures by calibrating positional attention biases.

research_basis.practical_implication: If you don't control placement, you are gambling. 'Context engineering' includes ordering, anchoring, and redundancy.
research_basis.source_note: References were reconstructed from primary research in November 2026; they are supporting sources, not recovered original search results. Findings are task- and model-dependent.

core_rules.why: Critical constraints buried mid-context are less reliably followed in long prompts.
core_rules.risk_if_ignored: Model violates non-negotiables (security, scope, budget, SoR ownership).

core_rules.rule: Put the output contract at the end.
core_rules.why: Recency helps: the last instructions steer formatting and deliverable compliance.

core_rules.rule: Never rely on a single mention of a critical fact.
core_rules.why: Position sensitivity causes intermittent misses; redundancy is a reliability technique.
core_rules.risk_if_ignored: Random failures across runs or after small context changes.

positional_design_patterns.name: Query Sandwich
positional_design_patterns.intent: Make the model repeatedly align to the task, reducing drift.
structure: Bottom: restated objective + explicit output contract
positional_design_patterns.use_when: RAG, long context, multi-doc analysis, policy-heavy tasks

positional_design_patterns.name: Anchor Tokens + Headings
positional_design_patterns.intent: Give the model strong navigational landmarks to stabilize attention.
positional_design_patterns.use_when: Enterprise architecture, SAP landscapes, governance-heavy work

positional_design_patterns.name: Critical Facts Duplication (CFD)
positional_design_patterns.intent: Repeat only the few facts that must never be missed.
structure: Place the same 3–7 critical facts in both: NON-NEGOTIABLES (top) and OUTPUT CONTRACT footer (bottom)

positional_design_patterns.name: Top-K + Diversity Retrieval
positional_design_patterns.intent: Avoid the 'more is worse' regime by controlling noise and redundancy.
structure: Retrieve N (e.g., 20) -> rerank -> keep top K (e.g., 5–8) -> ensure topical diversity -> order by relevance
positional_design_patterns.use_when: RAG systems, long-context Q&A, research synthesis
positional_design_patterns.research_hook: In the evaluated tasks, adding documents yielded diminishing returns.

positional_design_patterns.name: Middle Rescue: Extract-Then-Reason
positional_design_patterns.intent: Reduce dependence on middle context by forcing extraction first.
structure: Step 1: Extract relevant quotes/facts into a short 'Evidence Board' (<= 200 tokens)
Step 2: Reason ONLY over the Evidence Board
positional_design_patterns.use_when: When the model misses details in the middle or hallucinates connections

steps.acceptance: Each CFC is atomic, testable, and phrased as a rule.

steps.action: Place CFC at the top under NON-NEGOTIABLES.
steps.acceptance: CFC appear before any retrieved chunks.

steps.action: Insert evidence chunks; keep top K after reranking; delete near-duplicates.
steps.acceptance: Signal density is high; each chunk is used for a known purpose.

steps.action: Add a bottom footer with: task restatement + output contract + CFC repeated (CFD).
steps.acceptance: The model sees the contract last.

steps.action: Run a 'constraints recall check' before final answer.
steps.acceptance: If recall misses any CFC, you must re-anchor and rerun.

templates.constraints_recall_check: Before solving, restate NON-NEGOTIABLES as 5 bullets. If any are missing, ask clarifying questions instead of proceeding.
paca_skeleton: ### OUTPUT CONTRACT (JSON schema + required sections; repeat NON-NEGOTIABLES)

rules: Reason only over evidence_items. If something is missing, request it explicitly.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Retrieval Dump
anti_patterns.symptom: You append 15–50 chunks because the model supports long context.
anti_patterns.damage: Extra passages can add noise and cost; measure whether they improve the task.
anti_patterns.research_hook: In the evaluated tasks, adding documents yielded diminishing returns.

anti_patterns.name: Middle-Only Critical Detail
anti_patterns.symptom: The only mention of the key constraint sits inside a long evidence chunk.
anti_patterns.damage: A critical detail may be missed in a long context; position is one possible factor to test.

success_metrics.definition: Percent of runs where the model correctly restates all CFC before solving.
Percent of outputs that satisfy all CFC without manual correction.
How many provided chunks are actually cited/used by the model.
success_metrics.target: High; unused chunks are removed in next iteration.
